data.title: Investec Likely to See Slight Upgrades as Consensus Follows Guidance — Market Talk
data.description: Investec can expect slight upgrades as consensus on fiscal 2027 largely captures management's guidance, J.P. Morgan analyst Baron Nkomo says. Although the financial-services company's first-half results are positive--with adjusted EPS growth of 7.4% ahead of expectations--JPM stays neutral on the shares as it sees greater upside in other South African banks. The company offers reasonable EPS growth and a good return on equity, Nkomo says. The London-listed company is backed by a liquid, well-funded, and strongly capitalized balance sheet and well-positioned to drive profitable growth in specialist banking while scaling high-margin, capital-light businesses, the analyst adds. "We see resilient operating momentum, but near-term operating leverage remains constrained by elevated investment." Shares are down 7.5% at 554.50 pence. (anthony.orunagoriainoff@dowjones.com)

data.title: Rupee hits 7-month high at 93.33 against dollar as FPI buying, softer oil prices boost recovery
data.description:
The Indian rupee extended its winning streak on Thursday, November 19, reaching a seven-month high against the US dollar as continued foreign investor purchases and easing crude oil prices provided support to the domestic currency.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee strengthened to 93.3340 against the dollar, compared with its previous close of 93.4175, marking an appreciation of 7.75 paise.

The domestic currency began the session at 93.4000 and fluctuated between 93.1700 and 93.5500 during the day.

The recent appreciation has been driven by consistent foreign portfolio investor (FPI) participation in Indian equities, relatively cheaper crude oil and traders reducing their bearish positions on the rupee. However, a firm US dollar and the possibility of additional monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve remain potential headwinds.

What is driving the rupee's recovery?

  • Continued buying by foreign investors

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) maintained their positive stance on Indian equities for a 13th consecutive trading session on Wednesday. According to provisional exchange figures, they bought shares worth ₹5,866.78 crore.

These investments have contributed to higher dollar availability in the domestic foreign exchange market, providing support to the rupee.

  • Easing crude oil prices

Movements in international oil prices remain an important factor for the Indian currency, given the country's dependence on crude imports.

Brent crude, the global benchmark, was trading 0.26% lower at $91.71 per barrel in futures trade.

A moderation in oil prices can lower India's overall import expenditure and reduce the dollar requirement of domestic oil importers. This, in turn, eases demand for the US currency and provides some relief to the rupee.

  • Traders reduce bearish positions

Changes in currency market positioning have also helped the rupee gain ground. Market participants have been cutting back on bets against the Indian currency, triggering short-covering activity.

This reduction in bearish positions has added to the buying support for the rupee and contributed to its recent appreciation.

  • RBI initiatives and changing market positions

Measures introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), including initiatives to encourage foreign currency deposits, have also been identified by market strategists as factors supporting the domestic currency.

Additionally, the reduction of speculative long positions in the US dollar has helped ease pressure on the rupee.

What could limit further gains?

Despite its recent advance, the rupee continues to face risks from international monetary developments. The US dollar has remained relatively strong, with the dollar index trading close to a 19-month high.

Minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting highlighted policymakers' concerns about persistent inflation. Some officials indicated support for additional monetary tightening.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller has also proposed a 50-basis-point interest rate increase in December or a quicker pace of hikes in 2027.

Higher interest rates in the US could make dollar-denominated assets more attractive to global investors, potentially strengthening the greenback and restricting further gains in the Indian currency.

data.title: German Stocks Rise On Tech Boost; DAX Up 0.23%
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - German stocks gained some ground in positive territory Thursday morning, after posting losses in the previous three sessions. Tech stocks found support after Anthropic's IPO raised a record $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX's reported $75 billion offering.

The benchmark DAX, which climbed to 25,945.59 earlier in the day, was up 60.17 points or 0.23% at 25,817.00 a little over half an hour before noon.

Infineon Technologies climbed nearly 3.5%. Deutsche Bank, MTU Aero Engines, Siemens Energy and Hochtief gained 2%-2.5%.

Siemens moved up nearly 2% and Daimler Truck Holding advanced 1.8%. Commerzbank gained about 1.1% after the German government reached an agreement with UniCredit on the takeover of the lender.

BASF, Bayer, Brenntag, Heidelberg Materials, Gea Group, Continental, Merck, Adidas and Siemens Healthineers posted modest gains.

SAP drifted lower 2.1%. Henkel shed nearly 2%. Fresenius Medical Care and Rheinmetall lost 1.4% and 1.2%, respectivelyl. Vonovia, Hannover RE, Munich RE, Deutsche Boerse, Beiersdorf and Symrise lost 0.7%-1%.

In economic news, the euro area current account surplus remained unchanged in September, data from the European Central Bank showed. The current account logged a surplus of EUR 12 billion in September, broadly unchanged from the previous month.

The surplus on goods trade fell to EUR 14 billion from EUR 21 billion. Meanwhile, the services surplus rose to EUR 16 billion from EUR 13 billion.

In the twelve months to September, the current account surplus declined to EUR 248 billion from EUR 279 billion a year earlier. The surplus was equivalent to 1.5 percent of euro area GDP.

data.title: Coal India, ReNew among four firms receiving rare-earth magnet scheme LoIs; e-bus portal launched
data.description:
India on Thursday handed over letters of intent (LoIs) to four companies, including Coal India and ReNew, under its ₹7,280-crore rare-earth permanent magnet manufacturing programme, while launching a ₹3,435-crore digital payment-security portal aimed at protecting electric-bus operators from defaults by public transport authorities.

Union Heavy Industries Minister H D Kumaraswamy identified Coal India Limited, Prozeal Green Energy Limited, ReNew Private Limited and Midwest Energy Limited as the successful bidders receiving LoIs, following a review of industry preparedness and manufacturing capabilities under the Rare Earth Permanent Magnets (REPM) Scheme.

📍New Delhi Reviewed the Industry Preparedness and Capability Assessment under the Rare Earth Permanent Magnets (REPM) Scheme, along with my esteemed Cabinet colleague, Shri @BjpVarma avaru, Hon'ble Minister of State for Heavy Industries and Steel, senior officials of the Ministry and industry representatives. Also handed over Letters of Intent (LoIs) to the successful bidders — Coal India Limited, Prozeal Green Energy Limited, ReNew Private Limited and Midwest Energy Limited.

Under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi avaru, India is taking significant strides towards establishing a robust, self-reliant and globally competitive rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing ecosystem. This landmark initiative will strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities, reduce import dependence, enhance supply-chain resilience and advance the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. @MHI_GoI #REPM #RareEarthPermanentMagnets #AatmanirbharBharat #MakeInIndia #ViksitBharat

— ಹೆಚ್.ಡಿ.ಕುಮಾರಸ್ವಾಮಿ | HD Kumaraswamy (@hd_kumaraswamy) November 19, 2026

“This landmark initiative will strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities, reduce import dependence, enhance supply-chain resilience and advance the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat,” Kumaraswamy said

The announcements seek to address two vulnerabilities in India’s electric-mobility transition: dependence on imported critical components, particularly from China, and payment risks that can discourage private investment in electric public transport.

Separately, Kumaraswamy launched the PM-eBus Sewa Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) IT Portal alongside Minister of State for Heavy Industries and Steel Bhupathiraju Srinivasa Varma.

He said the mechanism would “strengthen investor confidence, enhance the financial viability of e-bus operations, mitigate payment-related risks and encourage wider participation in India’s electric mobility ecosystem.”

The ₹3,435.33-crore payment-security programme covers more than 38,000 electric buses for up to 12 years and has received an overwhelming response from all 27 participating States and Union Territories, according to the Minister.

Building a domestic magnet industry

The rare-earth magnet programme aims to establish 6,000 tonnes of annual integrated manufacturing capacity for sintered rare-earth permanent magnets, which are used in electric-vehicle traction motors, wind turbines, electronics and defence systems.

Although earlier information indicated that five manufacturers would be selected, Kumaraswamy’s latest announcement identified four LoI recipients. The status of any additional selection and the individual capacity allocations were not specified.

The scheme provides ₹6,450 crore in sales-linked incentives over five years and ₹750 crore in capital subsidies. Manufacturers are allowed two years to establish production facilities, followed by five years of incentives linked to magnet sales.

The selection process followed a global tender that attracted 20 bids, reflecting industry interest in building domestic capacity for a component whose production remains concentrated in China.

According to the International Energy Agency, China accounted for 91 per cent of global rare-earth refining and 94 per cent of sintered permanent magnet production in 2024.

Government data show China supplied between 84.8 per cent and 90.4 per cent of India’s permanent-magnet imports by quantity during 2022-23 to 2024-25.

India possesses an estimated 7.23 million tonnes of rare-earth oxide resources contained in monazite deposits. While the country has capabilities in mining, separation, refining and metal extraction, industrial-scale manufacturing of alloys and finished magnets remains a critical gap.

The programme seeks to bridge that gap by establishing integrated domestic manufacturing capacity, reducing reliance on imported finished magnets and strengthening supply-chain resilience for automotive and other industries.

Securing payments for electric buses

The payment-security portal addresses a different challenge: the risk of delayed payments by public transport authorities to private electric-bus operators.

Under gross-cost contracts, private operators procure and operate electric buses while transport authorities pay for services, generally on a per-kilometre basis. Payment delays can disrupt cash flows, increase financing costs and discourage lenders from supporting additional fleets.

Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL) manages the payment-security fund and reviews and verifies claims. If a public transport authority defaults, CESL can release an approved payment into the operator’s escrow account.

The authority must reimburse the amount within 90 days. If it fails to do so, the Ministry can seek recovery through the state’s direct-debit mandate with the Reserve Bank of India.

As of March 2026, 19 States and Union Territories had submitted direct-debit mandates under the PM E-DRIVE or PM-eBus Sewa programmes. At that time, the government reported no payment defaults and no claims processed under the mechanism.

The Minister’s latest statement confirms participation by 27 States and Union Territories, although it does not specify how many have completed the RBI mandate requirements.

The execution challenge

The two initiatives address different constraints on India’s clean-mobility expansion.

The magnet programme seeks to develop a domestic industrial supply chain for critical EV components, while the payment-security mechanism aims to make electric-bus contracts more bankable and attract private capital into fleet deployment.

Both face execution tests. The four LoI recipients must translate their proposed manufacturing projects into commercial production, while the payment mechanism’s effectiveness will depend on timely settlement and recovery of claims when defaults occur.

data.title: Anthropic investors’ shares rise ahead of Claude developer's record market debut
data.description:
Shares of major technology companies invested in Anthropic rose in premarket trading on Thursday as the AI startup prepared for its stock market debut.

Amazon shares gained 2.4%, while Alphabet rose 3.5%. Amazon's stake in Anthropic will amount to 14.7%, while Alphabet will own 13.7%. Both holdings will consist of non-voting shares.

Nvidia climbed 2%, AMD added 3%, and Broadcom advanced 2.9%.

Zoom Communications was up 2.5%, Microsoft up 1.4%, and Micron was up 4.2%. But Salesforce was down 0.16%.

The iShares AI Innovation and Tech Active ETF also rose 4% in premarket trading.

Anthropic priced its shares at $83 apiece, raising $81.3B, which is the largest stock market debut on record. The offering values the company at about $1.5T.

data.title: Mergers and acquisitions
data.description:
The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 1050 GMT on Thursday:

** UniCredit and Germany have reached a deal on the main sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, marking a major breakthrough in the two-year battle for control of the German lender.

** German media and services group Bertelsmann is buying Turkey-based Ekol Logistics for more than €500 million ($548 million), CEO Thomas Rabe said on Thursday, in a bet on the Turkish logistics market that he expects to grow 8% to 10% annually.

** French utility EDF will add about 1.3 million customer accounts to its UK retail business under an agreement to buy Luxion Group, owner of prepayment energy supplier Utilita Energy, EDF said.

** Cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks raised its annual revenue forecast and agreed to acquire AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion, as a heightened threat environment pushes customers toward broader security products.

** Challenger said it had received a revised takeover proposal from a unit of Daiichi Life for the remaining 79.5% of shares the Japanese insurer does not yet own, valuing the Australian investment manager at A$8.17 billion ($5.48 billion).

data.title: Euro zone bond yields hold steady as energy prices remain subdued
data.description:
Euro zone bond yields were little changed on Thursday as energy prices held steady, with investors looking to comments from European Central Bank officials and the APEC summit in China for clues about the outlook for the global economy.

Germany's 10-year bond yield (DE10YT=RR) rose less than 1 basis point to 3.385%. Yields move inversely to prices.

It has fallen in recent months from a 17-year high of 3.653% touched in late September as energy prices have cooled and a selloff in tech stocks has pushed investors towards safe-haven assets.

The focus of global financial markets was on the IPO of Anthropic , which has raised $81 billion in the largest stock-market debut on record, valuing the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion.

"Broader risk sentiment likely remains more relevant for longer rates [bond yields] than data releases," said Benjamin Schroeder, senior rates strategist at ING.

Oil prices held steady on Thursday, with Brent crude at $92 a barrel, as US President Donald Trump met with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China.

Trump had said they would discuss the conflict in Ukraine, which has had a major impact on European energy prices, and nuclear arms control.

President Christine Lagarde is among the European Central Bank officials set to speak later in the day as traders look for clues on interest rates.

Germany's 2-year bond yield (DE2YT=RR) rose 2 bps to 3.143%.

The spread between French and German 10-year bond yields – which has risen sharply this year – rose 1 bp to 150 bps (DE10FR10=RR).

Federal Reserve minutes released on Wednesday showed US policymakers saw a growing risk that they might need to step up their efforts to control inflation.

data.title: GPE reaffirms outlook after strong start to the year
data.description:
The London-focused office landlord saw revenues from its wholly-owned properties rise to £67.8m in the six months to 30 September, up from £54.6m, and earnings per share spike 43.6% to 5.6p, after it secured 40 new leases and renewals during the period generating annual rent of £19m per annum.

Like-for-like rental income growth was 11.9%, while rental values rose 2.1%.

The portfolio, which also includes retail space, was valued at £3.2bn, up 2.5%.

Toby Courtauld, chief executive, said: "We have delivered another strong half-year performance, with leasing and development driving earnings, values and returns."

Looking ahead, and GPE said its property capital value indicators had improved for rental growth but weakened marginally for yields, "reflecting a volatile macro backdrop" and elevated gilt rates, although investment market volumes remained stabled.

However, Courtauld said: "Despite continued economic uncertainty, record levels of demand for prime offices in central London and limited supply both support our rental growth guidance of 4% to 7%. With our fully managed operations expanding and exciting new schemes like Soho Square progressing, we are confident we will deliver our medium-term ambition of annual returns on equity of above 10%."

As at 1015 GMT, the FTSE 250 stock was largely unchanged at 352.2p.

data.title: Eurozone Construction Output Rises Marginally
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Eurozone construction output grew marginally in September after falling for four straight months, Eurostat reported Thursday.

Construction output rose 0.1 percent from August, when production dropped 0.5 percent. This was the first growth in five months.

Construction of building and civil engineering grew 0.7 percent and 0.8 percent, respectively. Meanwhile, specialized construction activities edged down 0.1 percent.

In the EU, construction output decreased 0.5 percent on a monthly basis and was down 1.4 percent in September from the last year.

Among member states of EU, the highest monthly increases in production in construction were recorded in Slovenia, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden. On the other hand, the largest decreases were observed in Hungary, Romania and Poland.

data.title: Alibaba Earnings Rebound Sharply as AI Profitability Improves
data.description:
By Tracy Qu

Alibaba Group recorded a surge in fiscal second-quarter profit as its AI profitability and e-commerce business improved.

The Hangzhou-based company has doubled down on artificial intelligence as a growth driver, a push that faces a new risk from heightened scrutiny about exports of chips to China. It has committed to spending more than $53 billion over three years to develop both the hardware and software that power AI.

Its success on that front holds the key to staying competitive amid challenges from other big tech firms and startups alike. But going all in on AI has proved a drag on profitability over recent quarters, putting pressure on Alibaba to deliver on its AI goals.

Its latest results look reassuring.

On Thursday, Alibaba said net profit tripled from a year earlier to 64.535 billion yuan, equivalent to $9.68 billion, for the three months ended September. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected 23.72 billion yuan. Revenue grew about 10% to 271.52 billion yuan, also better than market estimates.

Alibaba attributed the sharp profit improvement to higher net investment income and income from operations.

The earnings beat comes as Alibaba prepares a Hong Kong listing for its chip unit, T-Head, that investors view as a major validation of its efforts to produce in-house semiconductors. The business could fetch a valuation of $85 billion, according to Nomura estimates.

Write to Tracy Qu at tracy.qu@wsj.com

data.title: HK-listed Guangzhou Innogen signs over $1 billion licensing deal for diabetes drug
data.description:
Hong Kong-listed Guangzhou Innogen Pharmaceutical said on Thursday it signed a licence agreement worth more than $1 billion with Arcera Life Sciences to commercialise its GLP-1 ​receptor agonist drugs used to treat patients with type 2 diabetes.

The deal will allow Abu Dhabi-based Arcera to obtain regulatory approvals and commercialise the pharmaceutical product containing Efsubaglutide Alfa for human therapeutic use in selected countries in Africa, Latin America, the Middle East and Eastern Europe, Guangzhou Innogen said.

  • The China-based pharmaceutical products developer said its unit, Hong Kong Innogen Pharmaceutical, entered into the licensing deal with Arcera

  • Under the deal, Innogen could receive up to $38 million in upfront and near-term milestone payments, plus sales milestones and double-digit royalties tied to annual net sales

  • The board said the deal is in shareholders' best interests, leveraging Arcera's commercial network to accelerate the global expansion and value of Efsubaglutide Alfa

  • Arcera Life Sciences is a global pharmaceutical and biotechnology firm with operations spanning Africa, Europe, and parts of Latin America

  • The deal comes as global drugmakers race to secure next-generation diabetes and obesity treatments offering greater convenience, tolerability and efficacy

data.title: AM Need to Know: Anthropic prices IPO, Intel lands first 18A-P customer & more
data.description:
U.S. stock futures moved higher early Thursday, with technology shares leading the gains, as investors turned their attention to the highly anticipated public debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic.

Now, here are three news stories that broke overnight to watch out for:

Anthropic prices record $81.34 billion IPO above targeted range: Anthropic   priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above its marketed $70 to $78 range, with the offering comprising 980 million shares to raise approximately $81.34 billion. The combined offering surpasses SpaceX's $75 billion debut earlier this year to become the largest IPO on record. Shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT, with the offering expected to close on November 20.

Intel secures first external customer for 18A-P foundry process: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan  announced at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas, that the company has signed its debut outside customer for its 18A-P manufacturing process node, sending INTC shares 2.6% higher in extended trading. Intel's technology chief Pushkar Ranade clarified on X that the customer had signed up for the 18A-P node, which went into risk production in June. The deal marks a milestone in Intel's five-year effort to compete with chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. Reports in May indicated Apple and Intel were closing in on a deal to use Intel's foundry for some Apple device chips, though Tan did not name the debut client.

Wall Street's $500 billion Nvidia chip financing initiative stalls: A pledge from Wall Street firms to secure $500 billion in  financing for Nvidia chips has failed to materialize, according to the Wall Street Journal. Former CEO Jensen Huang secured commitments from Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR in August, with the capital intended for AI customers including OpenAI and Anthropic. No funds have been deployed, the Journal reported, and investor doubt is growing about whether the program will proceed following Huang's exit and the cautious stance of interim CEO Colette Kress, who said on Tuesday's earnings call that the company is "rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees."

AbbVie partners with DISCO Pharma in $2.54 billion cancer drug agreement: AbbVie has  agreed to pay up to $2.54 billion to collaborate with Germany-based DISCO Pharmaceuticals on developing novel cancer treatments using next-generation bispecific therapies. DISCO will receive $40 million upfront and up to $2.5 billion in milestone payments to develop AND-gated bispecific therapeutics for solid tumors, along with tiered royalties on worldwide net sales. The approach is designed to recognize cancer cells only when two target proteins are present simultaneously, potentially reducing damage to healthy tissue.

data.title: Italy antitrust closes Vorwerk probe after consumer compensation deal
data.description:
Italy's competition authority has closed its investigation into Thermomix maker Vorwerk after the company agreed to compensate consumers affected by problems with Neato robotic vacuum cleaners, it said on Thursday.

The Italian watchdog opened a probe in April into the home appliance maker over alleged unfair commercial practices for interrupting cloud services for its discontinued robotic vacuum cleaner Neato.

  • According to the regulator, Vorwerk would introduce significant financial compensation measures for owners of Neato robot vacuum cleaners affected by the practices under investigation, bringing the case to an end

  • Vorwerk will offer European consumers who purchased a Neato robot vacuum cleaner after October 1, 2020, either a replacement with its VR7 model for newer-generation devices or a €500 ($550) voucher redeemable against Vorwerk products for older models

  • The compensation scheme will apply across Europe, not just in Italy

  • Vorwerk has also committed to extending to 10 years the warranty covering digital services for its VR7 robot vacuum cleaners

  • Eligible consumers will be able to apply for either the replacement device or the voucher through online forms that the company will make available within three days

data.title: Ant International launches protocol for real-time settlement between tokenized deposits and money market funds
data.description:
Singapore-based fintech firm Ant International, which began operating independently following a 2024 reorganization of Ant Group, has launched the Whale Orchestration Protocol, an upgrade to its blockchain-based wholesale settlement platform.

In a Thursday press release, the company said the protocol was developed under the Monetary Authority of Singapore's BLOOM initiative to enable delivery-versus-payment transactions between tokenized deposits and tokenized money market funds.

Specifically, the protocol operates through WhaleRTP, Ant's blockchain-based wholesale settlement platform for real-time treasury and liquidity management. "This unlocks immediate liquidity for the company's real-time global treasury management, allowing idle capital to be deployed in real time," the company said.

Ant International also said it has completed pilot transactions with DBS and Franklin Templeton after the two integrated their respective Treasury Tokens and Tokenized Money Market Fund solutions into its WhaleRTP platform.

"As a full-stack financial solutions provider, 24/7 real-time liquidity management is essential for our business," said Kelvin Li, general manager of platform tech and SVP at Ant International.

Ant International is among the institutions participating in the BLOOM initiative, which the Singaporean central bank launched in October 2025 to develop approaches for settlement using tokenized bank deposits and stablecoins.

Tokenization drive

The launch comes as Singapore's central bank and major financial institutions step up efforts to develop tokenized financial infrastructure. The MAS announced Thursday that it issued S$100 million ($77.5 million) of four-week tokenized MAS Bills on Nov. 6. The bills were issued natively on its Singapore Dollar Test Network and settled in wholesale CBDC.

Also on Thursday, Standard Chartered announced an expansion of its tokenized deposits solution to enable near real-time transactions across Singapore and Hong Kong.

StraitsX, OCBC, and Standard Chartered also said on the same day that they have completed a trial examining interoperability between tokenized deposit networks issued by different banks.

Earlier this week, DBS Bank and Kinexys by JPMorgan also launched an interoperability solution designed to enable institutions to make instant transfers of USD tokenized deposits between the U.S. and Singapore.

data.title: Sweden's Vattenfall extends Ringhals 3 nuclear reactor outage again
data.description:
Swedish utility Vattenfall said on Thursday it is postponing the start-up of the Ringhals 3 nuclear reactor, which has been offline since May, by a further 16 days to December 20.

  • The latest delay was due to a leaky valve inside the reactor containment discovered during tests ahead of the start-up, previously scheduled for December 4

  • "The valve needs to be repaired before the reactor can be put into operation again," the state-owned company said in a statement

  • Vattenfall stopped the 1,081-megawatts (MW) reactor in May for maintenance work, expecting a restart in July but has since postponed the restart several times

  • Extended outages at several reactors have contributed to higher power prices in the Nordics this year, and have also weighed on Vattenfall's profits

  • Vattenfall owns 70% of the Ringhals power plant on Sweden's west coast, and Germany's Uniper owns the remaining 30%

data.title: NLC India Renewables files DRHP for IPO with ₹3,300 crore fresh issue
data.description:
NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), the clean energy subsidiary of public sector undertaking (PSU) NLC India, has filed the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI for its initial public offering.

The proposed IPO will be a combination of a ₹3,300 crore fresh issue and an offer for sale (OFS) of equity shares held by the Tamil Nadu-based lignite major.

NIRL develops, owns and operates renewable energy plants and generates revenue through the sale of power to central and state government agencies and public utilities. Its portfolio spans projects and technologies across the renewable energy ecosystem, including solar (ground-mounted, rooftop and floating), wind and hybrid power projects. It is also expanding into energy storage and emerging energy solutions, including BESS, Pumped Storage Projects and agreen hydrogen.

Out of the proceeds, ₹2,475 crore will be used for the pre-payment of certain outstanding borrowings with the rest earmarked for ‘general corporate purposes’. As on November 10, 2026, the company had outstanding borrowings (fund based) of ₹3,524.8 crore.

The company said in a statement that it is in consultation with its investment banking partners for a pre-IPO placement of up to ₹660 crore, prior to filing of the Red Herring Prospectus, the proceeds from which will be reduced from the fresh issue if successfully completed.

NIRL reported revenue from operations of ₹172.6 crore and profit after tax (PAT) of ₹45.4 crore for FY26. For the six-month period ended September 30, 2026, revenue from operations stood at ₹393.5 crore, while PAT was ₹151.6 crore.

As at October 31, 2026, the company’s total Project Portfolio and Project Pipeline capacity is 16,203.96 MW for solar, wind, hybrid and FDRE capacity and 8,238.30 MWh for BESS and PSP.

SBI Capital Markets Limited, HDFC Bank Limited, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities Limited and IIFL Capital Services Limited are the book running lead managers (BRLM) to the offer.
